summary: Akiko Kikuchi specializes in Buddhist studies and other fields. She studied at Minobusan University and held a professorship at Musashino University, both attested in 2026.

Akiko Murakawa is an Indologist. She studied under doctoral supervisor Harry Falk, supervisors Gerhard Ehlers, Masato Fujii, and Muneo Tokunaga, and teachers Werner Knobl, Yasuke Ikari, and Kazuhiko Yoshida.

Akiko Walley works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1994–2001) and Harvard University (~2001–2009), later holding a post at the University of Oregon (2009–2016).

Akimichi Eda specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Marburg (attested 2005) under Michael Hahn, and also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar.
Akio Donohashi (b. 1948) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1974) and served as a professor at Kobe University (1990–1991).

Akio Minoura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held an associate professorship at Otani University (attested 2007–2013), conducted research abroad at Stanford University (2012–2013), and is attested as faculty at Otani Academic Society in 2026.

Akio Tanabe (b. 1964) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–2006) and held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1993), Kyoto University (1998, 2004), and the University of Tokyo (professor, 2015).

Akira Fujieda (1911–1998) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. After studying at Kyoto University (~1931–1934), he served there from 1948 (professor in 1968), and was a visiting professor at the University of Copenhagen (1970) and UC Berkeley (1988).
Akira Hataya is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as professor emeritus at Otani University (attested 2014).

Akira Hirakawa (1915–2002) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Shoson Miyamoto. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1962–1975) and also held posts at Waseda, Komazawa, and Rissho universities.

Akira Miyaji (b. 1945) specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Nagoya University (~1964–1991), he served at Hirosaki University, Nagoya University (~1976–2007), the Shizuoka Prefectural Museum of Art, and Ryukoku University (2013).
Akira Momiyama (b. 1953) is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1972–1980) and served as a professor at Saitama University (~1994).

Akira Mukai (b. 1942) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral course and served as an assistant at Hokkaido University (attested 1978), later serving as a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

Akira Omine (1929–2018) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University and Heidelberg University, and held posts at Kyoto University (1959), Osaka University of Foreign Studies (1966–1973), Osaka University (1980–1992), and Ryukoku University (1992).

Akira Sadakata (b. 1936) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, and at the University of Paris (1963), later serving as associate professor and professor at Tokai University (~1969–2006).

Akira Saito (b. 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and the Australian National University, and held professorships at the University of Tokyo (2000–2016) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2016).

Akira Shimada works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi under Rajeev Lochan and under Daud Ali, later holding posts at the British Museum and the State University of New York at New Paltz.

Akira Suganuma (1934–2016) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Toyo University (~1959–1962), where he served as assistant (~1962–1967) and associate professor (1991–1994), and taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1981).

Akira Takeda (1930–2021) specialized in Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1949–1959) under Takeshiro Kuraishi, and later held posts at the University of Tokyo (1961–1991), Tokyo Woman's Christian University (~1977–1988), and Meikai University (~1988–2001).
Akira Yamada (1922–2008) was a philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi from ~1943 to 1946 and later held a post at Nanzan University (~1970–1972).
